## Hook

## The landscape

Where the pricing model is readable at all, no single pricing model leads: usage-based, per-seat, tiered SaaS plans each 1 of 6, but 3 of 6 companies give no pricing model signal — the bigger finding is the silence. The dominant GTM motion is sales-led (3 of 6).
The three themes that carry the category's messaging: autonomy / agents (5 of 6); ROI / cost savings (5 of 6); scale & enterprise readiness (5 of 6).

## Three companies, read closely

**Intercom Fin** — usage-based, hybrid (self-serve + sales), leads with integrations & ecosystem.
Their own words: "Fin AI Agent works seamlessly with any helpdesk, including Salesforce, HubSpot, and more"
[What this choice tells you about who Intercom Fin thinks the buyer is, and what it costs them.]

Their own words: "Backed by enterprise-grade security and scale"
[What this choice tells you about who Clay thinks the buyer is, and what it costs them.]

**Lindy** — per-seat, hybrid (self-serve + sales), leads with integrations & ecosystem.

## The thesis

3 of 6 publish no readable pricing model at all; the most common GTM motion is sales-led (3 of 6), and nearly everyone leans on autonomy / agents (5 of 6). Every theme is already claimed by someone; the wedge, if there is one, is in proof, not in positioning.
